t: Baekje grew from a Mahan statelet on the Han River into a kingdom of south-western Korea, ruled from Hanseong, Ungjin and Sabi.
Its court was celebrated for refined Buddhist art, metalwork and stone pagodas, seen in King Muryeong's tomb and the Baekje incense burner.
Baekje passed Chinese writing, Buddhism and skilled craftsmen to Yamato Japan, its closest ally, before falling to Silla and the Tang in 660.
dyk: King Muryeong's tomb at Gongju, found unlooted in 1971, held an epitaph stone naming the king, a rare case in which a Three Kingdoms royal tomb can be identified with certainty.
